title: Section 190 — Every member of unlawful assembly guilty of offence committed in prosecution of common object

content.overview: BNS s. 190 — Every member of unlawful assembly guilty of offence committed in prosecution of common object.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Common object (old 149). Every member of an unlawful assembly is guilty of the offence committed in prosecution of the common object, or which the members knew to be likely.
In student language: BNS s. 190 is the rule on “Every member of unlawful assembly guilty of offence committed in prosecution of common object”. The section provides that if an offence is committed by any member of an unlawful assembly in prosecution of the common object of that assembly, or such as the members of that assembly knew to be likely to be committed in prosecution of that object, every person who, at the time of the committing of that offence, is a member of the same assembly, is guilty of that offence. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 190 exists so that “Every member of unlawful assembly guilty of offence committed in prosecution of common object” has a closed legal test in Chapter XI — Of Offences Against the Public Tranquillity. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Unlawful assembly, common object, rioting, affray, and promoting enmity.

The provision in detail
190. If an offence is committed by any member of an unlawful assembly in prosecution of the common object of that assembly, or such as the members of that assembly knew to be likely to be committed in prosecution of that object, every person who, at the time of the committing of that offence, is a member of the same assembly, is guilty of that offence

enhancement.legalPrinciple: Codifies collective constructive liability, holding every participating member of an unlawful assembly liable for offences committed in prosecution of the common object or known to be likely.

essentialIngredients: The commission of an act or omission falling within the statutory description of Every member of unlawful assembly guilty of offence committed in prosecution of common object.
The existence of the requisite culpable mental state (intention, knowledge, rashness, or negligence) prescribed under Section 190.
The absence of any statutory justification, exception, or lawful authority under Chapter III (General Exceptions).
The resulting consequence or endangerment specified in the statutory formula of Section 190.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 190 carries forward the cornerstone doctrine of Section 149 of the Indian Penal Code. It establishes statutory constructive liability across two distinct limbs: (1) offences committed in actual prosecution of the common object; and (2) offences which the members of the assembly knew to be likely to be committed in prosecution of that object. Once an individual is proved to be a member of the unlawful assembly at the time the offence occurs, no separate personal overt act of violence is required—liability is shared equally by every member. The liability ceases only if a member genuinely dissociates from the assembly before the crime is committed.
examples: Teaching example (Standard application): An individual intentionally commits acts satisfying the statutory formula of every member of unlawful assembly guilty of offence committed in prosecution of common object under Section 190 without lawful authority. The individual is liable under BNS s. 190.

Teaching example (Absence of mens rea / Lawful exception): A person acts in good faith or without the requisite statutory mental element under circumstances recognized by law. The essential ingredients of Section 190 are not satisfied; no penal liability attaches.
distinctions: Section 190 (Common Object) vs Section 3(5) (Common Intention): Section 190 requires an unlawful assembly of 5+ persons with a Section 189 common object; Section 3(5) requires active participation with a pre-arranged plan among 2 or more persons.

Section 190 vs Section 103(2) (Mob Lynching): Section 190 imputes constructive liability for any crime; Section 103(2) is a direct, standalone hate-crime felony where 5+ persons commit murder on identity grounds.
problemApplication: Issue: Whether the accused is liable under BNS s. 190 for conduct relating to every member of unlawful assembly guilty of offence committed in prosecution of common object.
Rule: Under BNS s. 190, liability attaches upon proof of the statutory actus reus accompanied by the requisite mens rea without lawful justification.
Application: The evidence demonstrates that the accused performed the specified act with the required state of mind, satisfying all statutory ingredients of Section 190.
Conclusion: The accused is guilty of an offence under BNS s. 190 and subject to the prescribed punishment.
